note: Non-porcine recombinant lipases: adrulipase alfa (MS1819, yeast YLLIP2) went into patients on a duct-ligated minipig study and fell well short of PERT in CF; burlulipase and SLV339 reached phase 2 with no public disease-model data.
label: EPI (recombinant lipase replacement)

engagement.population: Unselected (EPI due to chronic pancreatitis or cystic fibrosis)
engagement.note: YLLIP2 (MS1819 lipase) 4-80 mg/d raised CFA from 60% to 85-90% in PEI minipigs, matching 1.2 g pancreatin; no patient data yet.
engagement.short: Yeast lipase restored CFA in minipigs
engagement.quote: Oral administration of milligram amounts of YLLIP2 significantly increased CFA values, similar to that of 1.2 g pancreatin, in a minipig model of PEI.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the minipig readout is coefficient of fat absorption, which has a direct human counterpart.

engagement.magnitude_basis: CFA change from off-enzyme baseline (+21.8 points at 2.2 g/d in 11 CP patients) vs minipig +25-30 points
engagement.confidence_note: Sponsor-reported only (announced 2018, restated in the 10-K for 2019); NCT03481803 (first posted 2018-03-29) has no posted results; no peer-reviewed paper found.
engagement.note: Phase 2a in chronic pancreatitis (NCT03481803): CFA rose a mean 21.8 points from baseline at 2.2 g/day MS1819.
engagement.short: CFA rose in patients, as in pigs
engagement.quote: the highest dose (2.2 grams per day) cohort of MS1819 showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful increases in CFA compared to baseline with a mean increase of 21.8%
engagement.judgement: CFA is both the model's readout and the trial endpoint; the uncontrolled phase 2a primary was safety, so its CFA rise is scored here as engagement, not efficacy. Dated 2018 (Oct 2018 announcement); src is the 10-K restating it. Paired by me.

dose.population: Unselected (EPI due to chronic pancreatitis or cystic fibrosis)
dose.note: Effective pig dose 4-80 mg/d YLLIP2; a separate in-vitro test-meal assay judged 10 mg equal to 100,000 USP pancreatin. No human exposure or margin stated.
dose.short: Pig dose only, no human target
dose.quote: From in vitro test meal experiments, the lipase activity of YLLIP2 (10 mg) was estimated to be equivalent to that of pancreatin (1200 mg; 100,000 US Pharmacopeia units) at pH 6.
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the in-vitro equivalence is a potency ratio, not a human regimen; the 2.2 g/d MS1819-SD clinical dose (a spray-dried powder of undisclosed lipase content) was a bridging dose from the CP phase 2a, not a model-stated target, so the two cannot be compared.

efficacy.population: Unselected (EPI due to chronic pancreatitis or cystic fibrosis)
efficacy.note: Minipig CFA on YLLIP2 (84.6-90.0%) matched pancreatin (90.5%), implying a non-porcine lipase could replace PERT.
efficacy.quote: Oral administration of milligram amounts of YLLIP2 significantly increased CFA values, similar to that of 1.2 g pancreatin, in a minipig model of PEI.
efficacy.judgement: The model's prediction is equivalence to pancreatin, which is what the CF trials tested.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: CFA shortfall vs pancreatin: minipig 0.5-6 points, OPTION patients 30.6 points (55.6% vs 86.2%)
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results table (primary outcome), not prose; the quote is the outcome title and arm means. No peer-reviewed publication found.
efficacy.note: OPTION crossover in CF-EPI: CFA 55.6% on MS1819 2.2 g/d vs 86.2% on PERT; OPTION 2 at 2.2-4.4 g/d also fell short of PERT. Dated to the OPTION 2 topline press release (31 Mar 2021), the earliest public comparison; registry results (2022) set the status. Combination design: the single-arm add-on trial of MS1819 on top of PERT (NCT04302662) is scored on its primary endpoint, CFA, which rose 6.57 points from baseline (topline 18 Aug 2021, interim 13 May 2021); it matches the model in direction but comes after this contra on the same track, so it changes no status and sits in patient_trials.
efficacy.short: CFA far below PERT in CF patients
efficacy.quote: Efficacy of MS1819-SD: Coefficient of Fat Absorption (CFA) [...] MS1819 55.6 [...] PERT 86.2

patient_trials.quote: MS1819 (2240 mg/Day) 66 [...] PERT (MS1819 2240 mg/Day Crossover Group) 83.3 [...] MS1819 (4480 mg/Day) 52.8 [...] PERT (MS1819 4480 mg/Day Crossover Group 89.3
Study to Assess an Enteric Microgranule Formulation of Adrulipase in Patients With Cystic Fibrosis
Data collected from 20 patients indicated that MS1819 in combination with PERT led to clinically meaningful improvements in the primary efficacy endpoint, the Coefficient of Fat Absorption.

efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: the sponsor announced OPTION as positive in Sept 2019 (about half of patients reached non-inferiority CFA), but the registry means show MS1819 far below PERT, so the higher-tier record sets contra, dated to its 2022 posting. CF-EPI patients count as the EPI disease. Paired by me; burlulipase and SLV339 have no public model data and do not enter this track.

efficacy.note: B. plantarii lipase cut steatorrhea dose-dependently in duct-ligated dogs; liquid beat powder; authors predicted it may abolish human steatorrhea.
efficacy.quote: The combination of adequate mixing of small amounts (milligrams) of bacterial lipase and high-fat meals abolishes canine steatorrhea and may abolish human pancreatic steatorrhea.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract plus full-text methods (scraped PDF): lipase was B. plantarii lipase from Knoll AG, the enzyme later developed as burlulipase; not the NM-BL liquid formulation itself.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. The dog enzyme is the same bacterial lipase (B. plantarii) that became burlulipase, so product_in_model true at medium confidence; the dog readout is CFA, the human primary endpoint.
efficacy.model: Pancreatic duct-ligated dogs (Mayo Clinic, DiMagno), dosed with Burkholderia plantarii bacterial lipase

efficacy.note: Phase 2a crossover in CF-EPI (NCT01710644): CFA 72.7% on burlulipase (NM-BL, liquid) vs 53.8% on placebo, as the dogs predicted in direction.
efficacy.short: CFA rose vs placebo in CF patients
efficacy.quote: During treatment with NM-BL, the coefficient of fat absorption was significantly greater (72.7%) compared with placebo (53.8%) with a difference between groups of 18.8% (P < .001).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); full text blocked. Registry NCT01710644 (first posted 2012-10-19) has no posted results.
efficacy.reason: Burlulipase raised CFA as dogs predicted
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me; the trial abstract does not cite the dog work. Direction matched, but the dogs' near-abolition of steatorrhea was not reproduced (72.7% CFA is far from normal), so magnitude is direction_only. CF-EPI counts as the EPI disease, as in the draft.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: CFA: dogs near-normal at 300,000-600,000 IU (240 mg); patients 72.7% vs 53.8% placebo
efficacy.model: Pancreatic duct-ligated dogs (Mayo Clinic, DiMagno), dosed with Burkholderia plantarii bacterial lipase

safety.population: Unselected (EPI due to chronic pancreatitis or cystic fibrosis)
safety.confidence_note: Toxicology package for the 2017 phase 2a and the 2018 IND is not public; patients had mainly mild GI adverse events (registry).
safety.note: GLP toxicology must have supported the 2017 phase 2a and 2018 US IND, but none is published; trials reported no serious adverse events.
safety.quote: In October 2018, the FDA cleared the Company’s Investigational New Drug (“IND”) application for MS1819 in patients with EPI due to CF.
safety.judgement: Year is a proxy: the phase 2a started January 2017, so the toxicology predates it. The minipig efficacy paper reports no safety readout.
